title: Quick check: Building Interactive Components

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Building Interactive Components”?
options: The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Buttons and toggles should connect an interaction to a handler without doing the action during render.
questions.answer_key: Buttons and toggles should connect an interaction to a handler without doing the action during render.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Building Interactive Components: Buttons and toggles should connect an interaction to a handler without doing the action during render.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Buttons and toggles?
options: Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
Use a semantic interactive element and pass a handler function rather than calling it during render.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
questions.answer_key: Use a semantic interactive element and pass a handler function rather than calling it during render.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Building Interactive Components: Use a semantic interactive element and pass a handler function rather than calling it during render.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Building Interactive Components” complete?
options: Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Building Interactive Components: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
